sections.h2: Where does Monroe County sit in central Georgia?
sections.html:
Monroe County lies on the fall line, where the Piedmont gives way to the coastal plain, and it belongs to the Macon metro area. The legislature created it on May 15, 1821, and named it for James Monroe, per Wikipedia. Forsyth is both the county seat and the largest city.

The county measures 398 square miles, of which 396 are land. Nearly all of it drains to the Upper Ocmulgee River, with one small southwestern corner, west of a line between Yatesville and Culloden, draining to the Flint. Interstate 75 and Interstate 475 cross it, along with U.S. 23, U.S. 41 and U.S. 341 and state routes 18, 19, 42, 74 and 83. Butts, Jasper, Jones, Bibb, Crawford, Upson and Lamar counties surround it.

Forsyth and Culloden are the two incorporated cities. Bolingbroke, Juliette and Smarr are census-designated places. One school system, the Monroe County School District, covers every address in the county, which keeps school questions simple for a seller and a buyer alike.

sections.h2: How fast has Monroe County grown, and what are homes worth?
sections.html:
Monroe County has grown quickly, adding about 14.5% to its population between the April 2020 base and July 2025, and the typical owner-occupied home is valued at $271,200 for 2020 to 2024, according to QuickFacts.

The 2010 count was 26,424, so the county has added about 5,600 residents since then. Of adults 25 and older, 27.0% hold a bachelor's degree or more, and 10.5% of people are in poverty. The average commute is 25.4 minutes.

sections.h2: Where do I pay and ask questions about Monroe County property tax?
sections.html:
The Monroe County Tax Commissioner works from 38 W. Main Street in Forsyth and answers at (478) 994-7020. The commissioner's site shows hours of 7:30 a.m. to 5:00 p.m. Monday through Friday, a drive-through window and a mailing address of P.O. Box 357, Forsyth, GA 31029.

The office describes its job as collecting. It bills real property, personal property, mobile homes, timber and motor vehicles, but it reports to neither the Board of Tax Assessors nor the Board of Commissioners, and it has no say over your value or your rate. Questions about value go to the Tax Assessors' Office at (478) 994-7038. Millage rates come from the Board of Commissioners and the Board of Education.

Bills go to whoever owned the property on January 1. If you bought or sold after that date, contact the tax office.

sections.h2: What payment options does the Monroe County tax office offer?
sections.html:
Monroe County takes checks, cash and cards at the counter, in the drive-through lane, by mail, in a drop box and through the county's online search and pay page. The office notice asks mailed payments to carry a postmark dated 12/20, the date the real estate bill is due.

  • Visa, MasterCard and Discover carry a 2.5% fee on the total.
  • American Express carries a 3% fee.
  • The drop box takes car tag, property tax and mobile home payments after hours, on weekends and on holidays.
  • Tag renewals can also be done on the Department of Revenue site or at a kiosk.

Only a U.S. Postal Service postmark counts as proof of an on-time payment for the current year. Meter-dated postmarks are not honored. For overdue bills, the office urges walking the payment in, especially after a levy or tax sale advertisement has begun. Mobile home tax is due April 1.

sections.h2: What happens if a Monroe County property tax bill goes unpaid?
sections.html:
An unpaid Monroe County bill leads to interest, penalties and eventually a lien called a FiFa. The office's FAQ says interest and a penalty are added to late balances, so ask the counter for the current amounts.

  • A 30 day notice of intent goes to the owner of record before a FiFa is issued, and payment in full within those 30 days stops it.
  • Once tax is more than 90 days late, a FiFa can be recorded on the General Execution Docket kept by the Clerk of Superior Court.
  • Paying the tax with fees, penalties and interest cancels the FiFa.
  • The office does not sell tax liens over the counter.

Partial payments are accepted in any number, but penalties and interest continue on the remainder, and any account with a balance can be liened. These records are public, and the tax office says it does not report to credit bureaus or control their updates. A seller with a lien should plan on a payoff letter before closing.

sections.h2: How do I question a Monroe County property value?
sections.html:
Start with the Board of Tax Assessors at (478) 994-7038, then file a written appeal within 45 days of the date on the notice if the answer does not satisfy you. The commissioner's FAQ says the appeal can rest on taxability, value, uniformity or a denied exemption, and it must name the method of appeal you want.

Owners may declare a proposed value by filing a return with the assessors between January 1 and April 1. If the board disagrees, a notice with its own figure arrives by mail. Fair market value is the full figure the board sets, and the assessed value that gets taxed is 40% of it, less any exemptions. A mill represents one dollar per $1,000 of assessed value.

sections.h2: Is there a homestead exemption in Monroe County?
sections.html:
Yes. The Tax Assessors' Office approves homestead applications, and you qualify by owning and living in the home on January 1. Once approved, you do not file again each year unless you move or the deed changes.

The tax office points owners to the assessors, at (478) 994-7038, for other exemptions and special assessment programs. Ask which of them fit your situation rather than assuming a neighbor's savings apply to you. The state also lets counties raise homestead amounts above the statewide minimum, so the local figure may differ.

sections.h2: Which Monroe County departments should a seller check before listing?
sections.html:
A seller should check planning and zoning, building inspections and code enforcement, all of which have pages on the county site, monroecoga.org. A house with an open permit or a code notice is easier to sell once those items are closed.

The county also lists a water department, recycling centers and a landfill, and it invited residents to a town hall on its 20 year comprehensive plan at the Monroe County Conference Center on October 27, 2026. Ask planning and zoning how the plan may affect a particular parcel. For deeds and liens on file, the Clerk of Superior Court is the office to contact; the tax office points owners there for warranty deed copies.

sections.h2: What happens to Monroe County tax when a house sells mid-year?
sections.html:
Because bills follow the January 1 owner, the seller usually receives the full-year bill even if the sale closes in spring. Georgia gives no partial-year refund, according to the Department of Revenue, so the contract and the settlement statement decide who ultimately pays what share.

Statements go to the homeowner and never to the mortgage company, though the tax office does send lenders on record a data file. If you have an escrow account, confirm with your lender that it plans to pay, and forward the bill if necessary. Ask the Monroe County tax office for a current balance before closing and for the status of any FiFa.

faqs.q: What phone number reaches the Monroe County tax commissioner?
faqs.a: (478) 994-7020 reaches the commissioner's office in Forsyth. Value questions go to the Tax Assessors' Office at (478) 994-7038.

faqs.q: Can I mail my Monroe County property tax payment?
faqs.a: Yes, as long as the envelope carries a U.S. Postal Service postmark dated on or before the due date. The office does not honor meter-dated postmarks.

faqs.q: Does Monroe County have a drop box for payments?
faqs.a: Yes. A drop box serves car tag, property tax and mobile home payments after hours, on weekends and on holidays.

faqs.q: Who gets the Monroe County tax bill after I sell?
faqs.a: The statement goes to whoever owned the property on January 1. If a sale happened after that date, tell the tax office so it can update its records.

faqs.q: How long can I appeal a Monroe County value?
faqs.a: You have 45 days from the date of the assessment notice. File in writing with the Board of Tax Assessors and name the appeal method you prefer.
